docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install all skills from this repository into the current project for your agent of choice:

Install
npx skills add https://github.com/iolanta-tech/nanopublishing --skill '*' -a claude-code # (1)!
  1. Some valid agent values include: claude-code, codex, cursor, and others.

Add -g if you want a global install instead of a project-local one.

docs.title: Example session
docs.text:
Claude Code Codex Cursor 
claude

codex --full-auto # (1)!
  1. Codex needs --full-auto here to permit access to cache directories.
cursor-agent # (1)!
  1. Or just use chat in Cursor IDE.
Dave Please write, in index.md, that Europa is a satellite of Jupiter, according to the International Astronomical Union. HAL 9000 Here you are. index.md
# Europa is a satellite of Jupiter

**Europa** is a natural satellite of **Jupiter**.

According to the **International Astronomical Union (IAU)**, Europa is one of Jupiter's moons.
Dave How do we express that one thing is a satellite of another? /find-url-for satellite of HAL 9000

Wikidata has wdt:P397 , but for readability we can mint a local predicate and declare it as a subproperty.

Dave Okay, let's rely upon wikidata. /semantify index.md, then. HAL 9000

I've added YAML-LD frontmatter and mapped the astronomy claim to linked data.

---
"@context":
  - https://nanopublishing.iolanta.tech/context/v0.yamlld
  - this:is-satellite-of:
      "@type": "@id"
    rdfs:subPropertyOf:
      "@type": "@id"

$nanopublication:
  $assertion:
    - $id: this:is-satellite-of
      rdfs:label: is satellite of
      rdfs:subPropertyOf: wdt:P397
    - $id: wd:Q3143
      this:is-satellite-of: wd:Q319

  prov:wasAttributedTo: wd:Q6867

npx:describes: wd:Q319
---

# Europa is a satellite of Jupiter

**Europa** is a natural satellite of **Jupiter**.

According to the **International Astronomical Union (IAU)**, Europa is one of Jupiter's moons.
Dave Okay, that looks fine. /nanopublish index.md. HAL 9000 It is published. The signed artifact remains beside the Markdown source.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The shared YAML-LD context for nanopub authoring in this site is:

https://nanopublishing.iolanta.tech/context/v0.yamlld

docs.title: Overall Skeleton
docs.text:
"@context": https://nanopublishing.iolanta.tech/context/v0.yamlld

$nanopublication:
  $assertion:
    # Assertion: what do we want to say?
    - $id: something
      is: kind of anything

  # Provenance: on which grounds do we assert the above? On whose authority?
  prov:wasAttributedTo: https://some-important-international.example.org

# Top Level: what can we say about the whole publication that we're writing?
npx:supersedes: URL of a previous publication

docs.title: this:
docs.text:
this: is the local prefix for entities defined inside the current nanopublication. In the shared context, it expands to the nanopublication's own namespace, so this:MyEntity means "the resource MyEntity in this nanopublication".

Use this: when you need a local identifier that belongs to the nanopublication you are writing, for example when the nanopublication introduces or embeds a new entity. Use an external IRI such as wd:Q319 when the entity already exists elsewhere.

$nanopublication:
  $assertion:
    - $id: this:MyEntity
      rdfs:label: My entity

npx:introduces: this:MyEntity

docs.title: Prefixes
docs.text:
The shared context defines these prefixes:

Prefix Expands to this: http://purl.org/nanopub/temp/np/ npx: http://purl.org/nanopub/x/ wd: https://www.wikidata.org/entity/ wdt: http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/ prov: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# rdfs: http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#

docs.title: npx:describes
docs.text:
States what the nanopublication is about.

$nanopublication: …
npx:describes: wd:Q319

docs.title: npx:supersedes
docs.text:
Declares that this nanopublication supersedes an older nanopublication.

$nanopublication: …
npx:supersedes: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: npx:invalidates
docs.text:
Declares that this nanopublication invalidates another nanopublication.

$nanopublication: …
npx:invalidates: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: npx:hasOriginalVersion
docs.text:
Points to the original nanopublication in a version chain.

$nanopublication: …
npx:hasOriginalVersion: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: npx:retracts
docs.text:
Marks a nanopublication as retracting another nanopublication.

$nanopublication: …
npx:retracts: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: npx:hasNanopubType
docs.text:
Assigns a nanopublication type.

$nanopublication: …
npx:hasNanopubType: npx:DraftNanopub

docs.title: npx:introduces
docs.text:
States that the nanopublication introduces an entity.

$nanopublication: …
npx:introduces: this:MyEntity

docs.title: npx:embeds
docs.text:
States that the nanopublication embeds an entity.

$nanopublication: …
npx:embeds: this:MyEntity

docs.title: npx:wasCreatedWith
docs.text:
Attributes creation to a software tool.

$nanopublication: …
npx:wasCreatedWith: https://example.org/tool

docs.title: npx:certifies
docs.text:
Expresses certification of another nanopublication.

$nanopublication: …
npx:certifies: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: npx:qualifies
docs.text:
Expresses a weaker qualification of another nanopublication.

$nanopublication: …
npx:qualifies: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: npx:approvesOf
docs.text:
Expresses approval of another nanopublication.

$nanopublication: …
npx:approvesOf: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: npx:disapprovesOf
docs.text:
Expresses disapproval of another nanopublication.

$nanopublication: …
npx:disapprovesOf: https://w3id.org/np/RA…

docs.title: prov:wasAttributedTo
docs.text:
Attributes the assertion to an agent or authority.

$nanopublication:
  $assertion: …

  prov:wasAttributedTo: wd:Q6867

docs.title: $assertion level
docs.text: The shared context defines no assertion predicates. Assertion predicates are domain-specific and usually come from a local overlay context.

docs.title: Data ranges
docs.text:
• DataRange

    The class of OWL data ranges, which are special kinds of datatypes. Note: The use of the IRI owl:DataRange has been deprecated as of OWL 2. The IRI rdfs:Datatype SHOULD be used instead.

  • ¬ datatypeComplementOf

    The property that determines that a given data range is the complement of another data range with respect to the data domain.

  • withRestrictions

    The property that determines the collection of facet-value pairs that define a datatype restriction.

docs.title: Individuals
docs.text:
• AllDifferent

    The class of collections of pairwise different individuals.

  • AllDisjointClasses

    The class of collections of pairwise disjoint classes.

  • AllDisjointProperties

    The class of collections of pairwise disjoint properties.

  • NamedIndividual

    The class of named individuals.

  • ≠ differentFrom

    The property that determines that two given individuals are different.

  • distinctMembers

    The property that determines the collection of pairwise different individuals in a owl:AllDifferent axiom.

  • members

    The property that determines the collection of members in either a owl:AllDifferent, owl:AllDisjointClasses or owl:AllDisjointProperties axiom.

  • sameAs

    The property that determines that two given individuals are equal.

docs.title: Assertions
docs.text:
• NegativePropertyAssertion

    The class of negative property assertions.

  • assertionProperty

    The property that determines the predicate of a negative property assertion.

  • sourceIndividual

    The property that determines the subject of a negative property assertion.

  • targetIndividual

    The property that determines the object of a negative object property assertion.

  • targetValue

    The property that determines the value of a negative data property assertion.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text:
• Annotation

    The class of annotated annotations for which the RDF serialization consists of an annotated subject, predicate and object.

  • AnnotationProperty

    The class of annotation properties.

  • annotatedProperty

    The property that determines the predicate of an annotated axiom or annotated annotation.

  • annotatedSource

    The property that determines the subject of an annotated axiom or annotated annotation.

  • annotatedTarget

    The property that determines the object of an annotated axiom or annotated annotation.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
• 🗑 DeprecatedClass

    The class of deprecated classes.

  • 🗑 DeprecatedProperty

    The class of deprecated properties.

  • 🗑 deprecated

    The annotation property that indicates that a given entity has been deprecated.

docs.title: Ontologies
docs.text:
• Axiom

    The class of annotated axioms for which the RDF serialization consists of an annotated subject, predicate and object.

  • Ontology

    The class of ontologies.

  • OntologyProperty

    The class of ontology properties.

  • imports

    The property that is used for importing other ontologies into a given ontology.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
• ✓ backwardCompatibleWith

    The annotation property that indicates that a given ontology is backward compatible with another ontology.

  • ✗ incompatibleWith

    The annotation property that indicates that a given ontology is incompatible with another ontology.

  • ⎗ priorVersion

    The annotation property that indicates the predecessor ontology of a given ontology.

  • versionIRI

    The property that identifies the version IRI of an ontology.

  • versionInfo

    The annotation property that provides version information for an ontology or another OWL construct.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
• Class

    The class of OWL classes.

  • ⊥ Nothing

    This is the empty class.

  • ⊤ Thing

    The class of OWL individuals.

docs.title: Property classes
docs.text:
• DatatypeProperty

    The class of data properties.

  • ObjectProperty

    The class of object properties.

  • ↥ bottomDataProperty

    The data property that does not relate any individual to any data value.

  • ↥ bottomObjectProperty

    The object property that does not relate any two individuals.

  • ↧ topDataProperty

    The data property that relates every individual to every data value.

  • ↧ topObjectProperty

    The object property that relates every two individuals.

docs.title: Property characteristics
docs.text:
• AsymmetricProperty

    The class of asymmetric properties.

  • ⇸ FunctionalProperty

    The class of functional properties.

  • ↣ InverseFunctionalProperty

    The class of inverse-functional properties.

  • IrreflexiveProperty

    The class of irreflexive properties.

  • ReflexiveProperty

    The class of reflexive properties.

  • SymmetricProperty

    The class of symmetric properties.

  • TransitiveProperty

    The class of transitive properties.

docs.title: Class expressions
docs.text:
• ¬ complementOf

    The property that determines that a given class is the complement of another class.

  • disjointUnionOf

    The property that determines that a given class is equivalent to the disjoint union of a collection of other classes.

  • disjointWith

    The property that determines that two given classes are disjoint.

  • ≡ equivalentClass

    The property that determines that two given classes are equivalent, and that is used to specify datatype definitions.

  • hasKey

    The property that determines the collection of properties that jointly build a key.

  • ⊓ intersectionOf

    The property that determines the collection of classes or data ranges that build an intersection.

  • oneOf

    The property that determines the collection of individuals or data values that build an enumeration.

  • ⊔ unionOf

    The property that determines the collection of classes or data ranges that build a union.

docs.title: Property relations
docs.text:
• ⇶ equivalentProperty

    The property that determines that two given properties are equivalent.

  • inverseOf

    The property that determines that two given properties are inverse.

  • ∘ propertyChainAxiom

    The property that determines the n-tuple of properties that build a sub property chain of a given property.

  • propertyDisjointWith

    The property that determines that two given properties are disjoint.

docs.title: Restrictions
docs.text:
• Restriction

    The class of property restrictions.

  • ∀ allValuesFrom

    The property that determines the class that a universal property restriction refers to.

  • hasSelf

    The property that determines the property that a self restriction refers to.

  • hasValue

    The property that determines the individual that a has-value restriction refers to.

  • onClass

    The property that determines the class that a qualified object cardinality restriction refers to.

  • onDataRange

    The property that determines the data range that a qualified data cardinality restriction refers to.

  • onDatatype

    The property that determines the datatype that a datatype restriction refers to.

  • onProperties

    The property that determines the n-tuple of properties that a property restriction on an n-ary data range refers to.

  • onProperty

    The property that determines the property that a property restriction refers to.

  • ∃ someValuesFrom

    The property that determines the class that an existential property restriction refers to.

docs.title: Cardinality
docs.text:
• cardinality

    The property that determines the cardinality of an exact cardinality restriction.

  • ⩽ maxCardinality

    The property that determines the cardinality of a maximum cardinality restriction.

  • maxQualifiedCardinality

    The property that determines the cardinality of a maximum qualified cardinality restriction.

  • ⩾ minCardinality

    The property that determines the cardinality of a minimum cardinality restriction.

  • minQualifiedCardinality

    The property that determines the cardinality of a minimum qualified cardinality restriction.

  • qualifiedCardinality

    The property that determines the cardinality of an exact qualified cardinality restriction.

A visualization for the RDF vocabulary that groups terms for properties, triples, containers, language values, compound literals, and values. Iolanta picks this nanopub up via iolanta:visualizes rdf: and renders the grouped terms when the user navigates to the rdf: namespace.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• → Property

    The class of RDF properties.

  • ∈ type

    The subject is an instance of a class.

docs.title: Triples
docs.text:
• ⦀ Statement

    The class of RDF statements.

  • ◉ object

    The object of the subject RDF statement.

  • → predicate

    The predicate of the subject RDF statement.

  • ○ subject

    The subject of the subject RDF statement.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
• ⊕ Alt

    The class of containers of alternatives.

  • ⊎ Bag

    The class of unordered containers.

  • ⋮ List

    The class of RDF Lists.

  • ⋯ Seq

    The class of ordered containers.

  • first

    The first item in the subject RDF list.

  • ∅ nil

    The empty list, with no items in it. If the rest of a list is nil then the list has no more items in it.

  • rest

    The rest of the subject RDF list after the first item.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
• 🌐 langString

    The datatype of language-tagged string values

  • 🌐 language

    The language component of a CompoundLiteral.

docs.title: Compound Literal
docs.text:
• ⊞ CompoundLiteral

    A class representing a compound literal.

  • ⇄ direction

    The base direction component of a CompoundLiteral.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
• value

    Idiomatic property used for structured values.

  • HTML

    The datatype of RDF literals storing fragments of HTML content

  • JSON

    The datatype of RDF literals storing JSON content.

  • PlainLiteral

    The class of plain (i.e. untyped) literal values, as used in RIF and OWL 2

  • XMLLiteral

    The datatype of XML literal values.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
• Class

    The class of classes.

  • Datatype

    The class of RDF datatypes.

  • Literal

    The class of literal values, eg. textual strings and integers.

  • ⊤ Resource

    The class resource, everything.

docs.title: Semantic properties
docs.text:
• ⤚ domain

    A domain of the subject property.

  • ⤙ range

    A range of the subject property.

  • ⊆ subClassOf

    The subject is a subclass of a class.

  • ⥹ subPropertyOf

    The subject is a subproperty of a property.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• 📃 comment

    A description of the subject resource.

  • isDefinedBy

    The definition of the subject resource.

  • 🏷 label

    A human-readable name for the subject.

  • ⧉ seeAlso

    Further information about the subject resource.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
• Container

    The class of RDF containers.

  • ContainerMembershipProperty

    The class of container membership properties, rdf:_1, rdf:_2, ..., all of which are sub-properties of 'member'.

  • ∋ member

    A member of the subject resource.
